CONTROL.name: Healthy Control
CONTROL.description: No known pathology. MRI is expected to show normal anatomy and signal characteristics for age.
keyFeatures: No focal lesions or mass effect.
Normal ventricular size and sulcal pattern.
No abnormal enhancement or edema.

SCHZ.name: Schizophrenia
SCHZ.description: Neuroimaging may be normal or show subtle structural changes. Findings are supportive, not diagnostic.
keyFeatures: Possible mild ventricular enlargement.
Subtle cortical or hippocampal volume changes.
No focal mass or acute lesion.

BIPOLAR.name: Bipolar Disorder
BIPOLAR.description: Structural MRI is often normal; changes are subtle and non-specific. Imaging is mainly used to exclude other causes.
keyFeatures: No focal lesion expected.
Possible subtle volume changes in limbic regions.
No abnormal enhancement or edema.

ADHD.name: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
ADHD.description: Structural MRI is typically clinicaly unremarkable. Research-level morphometry may show subtle volume reductions in circuits involving the basal ganglia and prefrontal cortex.
keyFeatures: No gross structural abnormalities or focal lesions.
Possible subtle reduction in total gray matter volume.
Potential volume differences in the caudate nucleus or cerebellum (research context only).

HGG.name: High-Grade Glioma (HGG)
HGG.description: High-grade gliomas, including Glioblastoma (GBM), are aggressive primary brain tumors characterized by rapid cell proliferation, necrosis, and infiltrative growth into surrounding brain tissue.
keyFeatures: Irregular ring enhancement after contrast (gadolinium) administration.
Presence of central necrotic areas (low signal on T1ce, high on T2).
Extensive peritumoral edema (high signal on FLAIR/T2).
Frequent mass effect on adjacent brain structures.

LGG.name: Low-Grade Glioma (LGG)
LGG.description: Low-grade gliomas are slower-growing tumors that often appear well-differentiated. They lack the necrotic features of HGG but still have the potential to transform into high-grade tumors over time.
keyFeatures: Usually non-enhancing or minimal enhancement on T1ce.
Hyperintense signal on T2 and FLAIR images.
Relatively well-defined margins compared to HGG.
Less pronounced peritumoral edema and mass effect.
